mx-b01-n01.text: This is not accent removal. It is a four-movement repair kit for the words you already know. Equal taps keep every syllable alive. A flat palm stops English vowels from sliding. One small punch marks the stressed syllable. A finger flick replaces the heavy English R. We will use all four in the three places where your first words matter: the airport taxi, the hotel desk and a market counter.

mx-b01-n02.text: Now pay every syllable. English hides weak vowels; Mexican Spanish keeps them available. Tap once for each syllable, all taps the same size: cho-co-la-te. Four taps, then one small punch on LA: cho-co-LA-te.

mx-b01-p01.text: At a market counter, point to the chocolate and say what you want. Four equal taps and one punch on LA. Speak now.

mx-b01-n03.text: At the airport, the familiar word hotel is the trap. English hits HO; Spanish hits TEL. Give the word one short punch at the end: ho-TEL. Then stop. No extra vowel after the L.

mx-b01-t03.text: Al hotel del Centro Histórico, por favor.

mx-b01-p02.text: The authorised taxi driver asks where you are going. Give the destination and punch the end of ho-TEL. Speak now.

mx-b01-p03.text: The driver checks whether you want the main entrance. Confirm and thank him. Keep the S in gracias: Mexican Spanish does not use the Spanish th here. Speak now.

mx-b01-n04.text: That S matters to the identity of this course. In Mexico, gracias, cinco and zapato all use an S sound. The th taught for central Spain does not belong in the Mexican model. And LL and Y share one sound here: start with the Y in yes. You do not need a regional performance; you need a stable, recognisable word.

mx-b01-p04.text: At hotel reception, the clerk asks how she can help. Say that you have a reservation. Keep every syllable in reservación and punch the final syllable. Speak now.

mx-b01-p05.text: The clerk asks under what name. Say: under the name Morgan. Do not add an English R after the final vowel. Speak now.

mx-b01-s01.text: Al hotel del Centro Histórico, por favor. Sí, gracias. Tengo una reservación.

mx-b01-n05.text: B01 complete. Equal taps, flat palm, one punch, quick flick. You used them to buy something at a market, direct an airport taxi and open your hotel reservation. Your floor is not a Mexican accent. It is five steady vowels and every syllable present when the useful sentence leaves your mouth.

mx-b01-q-i.text: You have landed in Mexico. Listen to one short taxi exchange and one hotel exchange. Catch the destination, the confirmation and the reservation — not every sound.

mx-b01-q02.text: Al hotel del Centro Histórico, por favor.

mx-b02-n01.text: In Mexico, the useful politeness is not a long sentence. It is timing. The greeting comes before you inspect the shop. Con permiso comes before your body crosses someone else's space. Gracias and hasta luego arrive before the door closes. Five short pieces, each placed one second earlier than an English speaker expects.

mx-b02-p01.text: You open the door of a small shop in the morning. Before looking at the shelves, greet the person at the counter. Speak now.

mx-b02-n02.text: Dígame means the floor is yours. It is not a request for your life story. If you are only looking, say so and release the attendant from hovering.

mx-b02-p02.text: The shopkeeper asks how she can help, but you only want to look. Say that, and thank her. Speak now.

mx-b02-n03.text: Now the body move. A crowded lift, a narrow taquería aisle, somebody blocking the doorway: say con permiso before you squeeze through. You are not apologising for existing; you are announcing the movement before it happens.

mx-b02-p03.text: The lift doors open and one person is standing across the exit. Ask permission before moving past. Speak now.

mx-b02-p04.text: They make room and say pásele. Thank them as you pass. Speak now.

mx-b02-n04.text: Last move: close the exchange. Hasta luego does not promise you will return later. It is the ordinary sign-off as you leave a shop or counter.

mx-b02-p05.text: You have paid at a taquería and are walking out. Thank them and sign off before the door closes. Speak now.

mx-b02-p06.text: They answer que le vaya bien. Return the wish with one word. Speak now.

mx-b02-n05.text: B02 complete. Buenos días before the request. Con permiso before the body moves. Gracias when the space opens. Hasta luego before the door closes. If somebody answers pásele, dígame or que le vaya bien, you now know exactly where the exchange is going.

mx-b02-q-i.text: Listen to three tiny exchanges: a shop entrance, a blocked lift door and the end of a meal. The test is timing — what comes before the request or movement.

mx-b03-n01.text: The dangerous tourist sentence is the smile that means nothing. You miss a price or a street name, nod anyway and inherit the wrong problem. B03 gives you a four-step ladder: say the break, ask for slower repetition, move the detail into writing, then put the route on a map. You are not asking the person to become your teacher. You are changing the channel until the information survives.

mx-b03-p01.text: At a noisy counter, the attendant gives you a long answer and you lose it. Stop the false smile and say you didn't understand. Speak now.

mx-b03-n02.text: You may hear mande in Mexico when somebody did not catch you. Recognise it; you do not need to copy it. Your next step is explicit: repeat it more slowly. One request, not two separate apologies.

mx-b03-p02.text: The bus attendant repeats at the same speed. Ask for the whole thing again, more slowly. Speak now.

mx-b03-r02.text: Claro. Sale a las quince cincuenta.

mx-b03-n03.text: Slower can still fail when the payload is a number, surname or address. Stop spending listening attempts. Put the detail somewhere your eyes can hold it.

mx-b03-p03.text: You still cannot separate quince from cincuenta. Ask the attendant to write the departure time. Speak now.

mx-b03-n04.text: Last channel: the map. A written street name can still leave you with three branches and no idea which way to move. Hand over the phone already open on the map and ask for the point, not another paragraph.

mx-b03-p04.text: A local writes the street name, but you still do not know which branch it is. Open the map and ask them to show you. Speak now.

mx-b03-r04.text: Sí. Es aquí, después de la esquina.

mx-b03-s01.text: No entendí. ¿Me lo puede repetir más despacio? ¿Me lo puede escribir?

mx-b03-n05.text: B03 complete. Say the break. Slow the repeat. Write the payload. Point to the route. The ladder keeps the exchange in Spanish while removing the exact part your ears cannot carry yet.

mx-b03-q-i.text: A bus-counter answer arrives too fast. Listen to the traveller climb only as far as necessary: signal the break, slow it down, then write the departure time.

mx-b03-q01.text: Sale a las quince cincuenta por la entrada del fondo.

mx-b03-q02.text: No entendí. ¿Me lo puede repetir más despacio?

mx-b03-q03.text: Claro. Sale a las quince cincuenta.

mx-b04-n01.text: Tomorrow's flight does not begin at the airport. Put the passport book in your hand tonight and check that it covers the whole trip. A passport card cannot board the flight to Mexico. Check the airline's own validity rule too; Mexico's rule and an airline's boarding check are not the same thing.

mx-b04-n02.text: For a U.S. citizen visiting as a tourist for under one hundred eighty days, Mexico does not require a visa. That number is a ceiling, not a promise: immigration decides the authorised stay when you arrive. At an international airport, do not hunt for an old paper tourist form. The FMM is generated in the entry process; if an e-gate gives you a QR receipt, keep it with the passport.

mx-b04-n03.text: Now make the trip survive a dead phone. Save the hotel confirmation, full address and return booking offline. Immigration may ask for booking or itinerary evidence. Install the eSIM according to the provider's instructions and keep the activation steps offline. Carry two payment methods you have checked yourself. These are resilience tasks, not immigration requirements.

mx-b04-n04.text: The weak file is usually the hotel: a booking exists, but the name, arrival hour or full address is wrong. Confirm it before you fly, while changing it is still cheap.

mx-b04-p01.text: You message the hotel before flying. Open with the job: you want to confirm your reservation. Speak now.

mx-b04-n05.text: Do not settle for a green checkmark inside an app. Ask for a confirmation you can save outside it.

mx-b04-p02.text: The hotel finds your name. Ask them to send the confirmation by email so you can save it offline. Speak now.

mx-b04-t02.text: ¿Me puede mandar la confirmación por correo?

mx-b04-n06.text: A hotel name is not a destination. Your driver and your offline map need the complete address, including the neighbourhood when the city repeats street names.

mx-b04-p03.text: The confirmation shows only the hotel name. Ask for the complete address. Speak now.

mx-b04-n07.text: Last check: your flight lands late. A valid booking can still fail if the front desk closes before you arrive. Put the late arrival into the conversation now.

mx-b04-p04.text: You expect to reach the hotel after ten at night. State that, then ask whether reception is open twenty-four hours. Speak now.

mx-b04-t04.text: Llego después de las diez. ¿Hay recepción las veinticuatro horas?

mx-b04-s01.text: Quiero confirmar mi reservación. ¿Cuál es la dirección completa?

mx-b04-n08.text: B04 complete. Passport book checked. Entry evidence saved offline. Connection instructions available without connection. Two payment methods checked. Reservation, full address and late arrival confirmed. Recheck the dated entry rules before departure; the course records when each one must be reviewed.

mx-b04-q-i.text: A traveller checks the hotel the night before flying. Listen for the three details that make the reservation usable after the phone loses signal.

mx-b04-q03.text: ¿Me puede mandar la confirmación por correo? ¿Cuál es la dirección completa?

mx-b04-q04.text: Llego después de las diez. ¿Hay recepción las veinticuatro horas?

mx-b05-n01.text: The immigration desk is not a Spanish exam and it is not the place to improve your story. The officer determines the period you are authorised to stay. Listen for three jobs only: why you came, how long you will stay and where you will sleep. Give the true answer, then stop.

mx-b05-r01.text: ¿Cuál es el motivo de su viaje?

mx-b05-p01.text: The officer asks the purpose of the trip. You are travelling for a holiday. Answer in one sentence. Speak now.

mx-b05-n02.text: Use your real number. Ten days is the rehearsal value, not a line to memorise for every trip. Immigration can corroborate the length and purpose with your booking, return ticket or itinerary.

mx-b05-p02.text: Your actual itinerary is ten days. Give only the duration. Speak now.

mx-b05-n03.text: The accommodation answer is not the story of how you found the hotel. Name the category and let the saved reservation hold the address.

mx-b05-p03.text: The officer asks where you will stay. Your confirmed accommodation is the hotel shown in your offline reservation. Answer briefly. Speak now.

mx-b05-p04.text: The officer asks for proof. Hand over the offline confirmation without adding a speech. Speak now.

mx-b05-s01.text: Vengo de vacaciones. Diez días. Me hospedo en este hotel.

mx-b05-n04.text: B05 complete. Purpose: vacation. Duration: your real number. Accommodation: the place on your confirmed booking. If proof is requested, hand it over. Short does not mean evasive; short means the answer matches the question.

mx-b05-q-i.text: At Mexican immigration, the officer asks purpose, duration and accommodation. Listen for the clean stop after each answer.

mx-b05-q01.text: ¿Cuál es el motivo de su viaje?

mx-b05-q05.text: ¿Dónde se va a hospedar? ¿Tiene la reservación?

mx-b05-q06.text: Me hospedo en este hotel. Aquí tiene mi reservación.

mx-b06-n01.text: Your first hour has an order. A missing bag stays at the airline desk. Connection gets tested before you need the car. Payment gets asked before you hunt for cash. Bathroom and meeting point get solved with a person wearing airport identification. Transport begins only after those loose problems are closed.

mx-b06-p01.text: The carousel stops and your bag is absent. Before leaving the baggage area, tell the airline desk exactly what failed. Speak now.

mx-b06-n02.text: Next, test the eSIM you prepared in B04. If data does not appear, do not wander while repeatedly refreshing the phone. Ask for the airport network as one complete phrase. Hay is only a preview here; B08 will open the pattern.

mx-b06-p02.text: Your eSIM is installed but no data appears. Ask an information-desk employee whether there is wifi. Speak now.

mx-b06-r02.text: Sí. La red está en el letrero.

mx-b06-n03.text: Now the reusable engine: puedo plus an action. Puedo means can I; the second piece is the job. Use the bathroom. Pay by card. Wait here. Same opening, three different first-hour decisions.

mx-b06-p03.text: The nearest bathroom appears to be beyond a staffed barrier. Ask the employee whether you can use it. Speak now.

mx-b06-p04.text: At the small airport counter, you want water but do not know whether you need cash. Keep puedo and change the action: ask whether you can pay by card. Speak now.

mx-b06-n04.text: Last loose problem: your pickup has not appeared. Do not drift toward an unofficial offer. Choose a visible meeting point near identified staff and ask whether waiting there is allowed.

mx-b06-p05.text: Your pickup message says to wait by the information desk. Ask the identified employee whether you can wait there. Speak now.

mx-b06-s01.text: ¿Puedo usar el baño? ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta? ¿Puedo esperar aquí?

mx-b06-n05.text: B06 complete. Missing bag before you leave. Connection before you need the ride. Ask whether card works before chasing cash. Bathroom and waiting point through puedo plus the action. The first hour becomes five closed loops, not one large arrival panic.

mx-b06-q-i.text: The traveller still has four loose problems: a missing bag, no data, a payment question and a delayed pickup. Put them in the order that prevents one problem from travelling into the next.

mx-b07-n01.text: B06 left you at a stable information point. B07 begins with a channel, not a car. Airport systems vary across Mexico, so do not memorise a company, colour or door number. Ask identified staff where authorised transport is, then choose the taxi channel, the app pickup point or another official option before following a person.

mx-b07-p01.text: At the information desk, ask where the authorised transport is. Speak now.

mx-b07-r01.text: Al fondo, junto a la salida.

mx-b07-n02.text: If you chose an app, the car may not be allowed to collect you at the nearest door. Keep the booking inside the app and ask for the designated meeting point instead of accepting a replacement ride.

mx-b07-p02.text: Your app shows a confirmed ride but the pickup zone is unclear. Ask where the app meeting point is. Speak now.

mx-b07-t02.text: ¿Dónde está el punto de encuentro de la aplicación?

mx-b07-n03.text: For a quoted ride, put the destination into the question before entering. Show the offline address from B04 and ask the cost to that exact point. You do not need to produce the number; listen, read the display or use the calculator escape hatch.

mx-b07-p03.text: At the authorised counter, show the saved hotel address and ask the cost to that address before accepting. Speak now.

mx-b07-n04.text: Now the driver gets the same offline address. Do not retell the hotel name from memory; put the shared object between you.

mx-b07-p04.text: You are with the confirmed driver. Show the saved address and give that destination. Speak now.

mx-b07-n05.text: At the hotel entrance, close the route before opening the hotel problem. Aquí está bien stops the car at the usable point. The receipt preserves the ride channel, time and amount if something needs to be checked later.

mx-b07-p05.text: The car reaches the hotel entrance. Say this point is fine and ask for a receipt. Speak now.

mx-b07-t05.text: Aquí está bien. ¿Me da un recibo, por favor?

mx-b07-s01.text: ¿Cuánto cuesta hasta esta dirección? A esta dirección, por favor. Aquí está bien.

mx-b07-n06.text: B07 complete. Choose the authorised channel before the vehicle. Find the app meeting point instead of improvising a pickup. Put the exact address into the quote and the ride. Stop at the usable entrance and keep the receipt. You are at the bed; B08 begins outside it.

mx-b07-q-i.text: The airport allows more than one transport channel, but the pickup rules vary. Listen for the sequence that survives those differences: authorised channel, exact address, quote, stop and receipt.

mx-b07-q02.text: Al fondo, junto a la salida.

mx-b07-q05.text: Aquí está bien. ¿Me da un recibo, por favor?

mx-b08-n01.text: A stranger can answer where is the pharmacy with three streets, two corners and a hand wave. Start smaller. Hay asks whether the thing exists nearby. That first answer is yes or no, and yes or no fits in your head.

mx-b08-p01.text: You need medicine but do not know whether this street has a pharmacy. Ask the yes-or-no existence question first. Speak now.

mx-b08-r01.text: Sí, hay una en la esquina.

mx-b08-n02.text: The opening stays; the thing changes. You are looking for any cash machine, not a particular machine. Keep hay and replace only the object.

mx-b08-p02.text: You need any cash machine nearby. Keep the existence opening and replace the object. Speak now.

mx-b08-n03.text: Now the defined place. Inside this café there is one bathroom; you are not asking whether bathrooms exist in the neighbourhood. Dónde está asks where the known place is.

mx-b08-p03.text: In a café, ask where the bathroom is. It is the known place inside this building. Speak now.

mx-b08-n04.text: Dónde hay combines the two jobs when you want the location of any useful instance. The pharmacy is a category; any nearby one can solve the problem.

mx-b08-p04.text: The person confirmed that pharmacies exist nearby. Now ask where you can find one. Speak now.

mx-b08-r03.text: Siga derecho, cruce la avenida y dé vuelta después del mercado.

mx-b08-n05.text: That answer is too large. Do not ask for the same paragraph again. Collapse it into distance. If it is near, follow the arm and confirm the first landmark. If it is far, move the route onto the map.

mx-b08-p05.text: The stranger gives you three movements and you lose the middle. Ask only whether it is far. Speak now.

mx-b08-p06.text: Two blocks still leaves you unsure which turn begins the route. Open the map and ask the person to show you. Speak now.

mx-b08-r05.text: Sí. Es aquí, en esta esquina.

mx-b08-s01.text: ¿Hay una farmacia por aquí? ¿Dónde hay una farmacia? ¿Está lejos?

mx-b08-n06.text: B08 complete. Hay asks whether one exists. Dónde está finds the known place. Dónde hay finds any useful instance. Está lejos collapses a paragraph into a decision. The map takes over when words stop moving your feet.

mx-b08-q-i.text: A traveller needs a pharmacy in a historic-centre street. Listen as the question grows only when the previous answer is still usable.

mx-b08-q02.text: Sí, hay una en la esquina.

mx-b08-q04.text: Siga derecho, cruce la avenida y dé vuelta después del mercado.

mx-b08-q05.text: ¿Está lejos? ¿Me lo muestra en el mapa?

mx-b08-q06.text: No. Está a dos cuadras. Es aquí.

mx-b09-n01.text: Mexico has no single national city-transport ritual. Some systems use a paper ticket, some a card, some an app; validation and transfers change by city and operator. Your sequence does not change: destination, ticket, rule, platform, vehicle.

mx-b09-p01.text: Before buying anything, confirm whether this service goes downtown. Speak now.

mx-b09-r01.text: Sí, pero tiene que hacer transbordo.

mx-b09-n02.text: Now buy for the destination, not for a word like single that may not match the local product. In Mexico, boleto is the useful ticket word here.

mx-b09-p02.text: At the staffed counter, ask for one ticket to downtown. Speak now.

mx-b09-t02.text: Un boleto para el centro, por favor.

mx-b09-n03.text: The ticket exists; the rule is still unknown. Tengo que asks what obligation belongs to you. Keep the opening and attach the action: validate the ticket.

mx-b09-p03.text: You have the ticket, but there is a reader before the platform. Ask whether you must validate it. Speak now.

mx-b09-n04.text: Do not decode the machine from a distance. Follow the hand, validate, then find the platform if this station uses one. B08 already gave you the defined-location question.

mx-b09-p04.text: The ticket is valid, but you still need the platform for this departure. Ask where the platform is. Speak now.

mx-b09-n05.text: The opening returns with a different action. The destination is correct, but the first answer said transfer. Ask whether that obligation belongs to this journey.

mx-b09-p05.text: At the platform, ask whether you have to make a transfer on the way downtown. Speak now.

mx-b09-n06.text: Last check happens at the door, not after it closes. Show the destination and confirm this bus. The line number can stay on the sign; you do not need to perform it from memory.

mx-b09-p06.text: The bus arrives at the platform. Before boarding, confirm that this vehicle goes to the Historic Centre. Speak now.

mx-b09-s01.text: ¿Tengo que validar el boleto? ¿Tengo que hacer transbordo?

mx-b09-n07.text: B09 complete. Destination before purchase. Boleto in Mexico. Ask the validation rule instead of guessing. Find the platform. Ask whether transfer belongs to this journey. Confirm the vehicle at the door. The line number can stay on the screen; your job is the sequence.

mx-b09-q-i.text: A traveller needs local transport to the Historic Centre. Listen for the two different destination checks and the two obligations discovered in between.

mx-b09-q02.text: Sí, pero tiene que hacer transbordo.

mx-b09-q03.text: Un boleto para el centro, por favor. ¿Tengo que validar el boleto?

mx-b10-n01.text: B10 is a silent lesson. You will not pronounce, spell or copy a sign. You will recognise a short surface and move: enter, leave, pull, push, queue, find the toilets, check the time or stop.

mx-b10-n02.text: At a divided doorway, choose the flow before you reach it. Entrada takes you in. Salida takes you out. The arrow and the people confirm the word; do not stop in the crossing to translate it.

mx-b10-n03.text: On a manual door in Mexico, jale brings the door toward you and empuje sends it away. Eyes reach the word before the hand reaches the handle. Automatic doors need no reading ritual.

mx-b10-n04.text: Fila tells you where the waiting begins. Taquilla tells you what the window does. If the queue ends at that window, join the back instead of walking to the glass and asking everyone.

mx-b10-n05.text: Both surfaces can lead to the toilets. Follow the pictogram and arrow. If neither surface exists, use the location question from B08; the sign lesson does not replace the repair route.

mx-b10-n06.text: Horario introduces the times that apply to that place. Match today with its range; do not import a national opening pattern. Cerrado ends the decision for now: change time or place before asking for service.

mx-b10-n07.text: Último acceso is the deadline to enter, not necessarily the time the whole place closes. Solo personal marks a boundary: stop and use a public route. One sign protects time; the other protects access.

mx-b10-n08.text: B10 complete. Entrance or exit. Pull or push. Back of the queue or ticket window. Toilets. Today’s hours. Last entry. Staff only. No speaking test and no copied alphabet: surface, decision, body.

mx-b10-q-i.text: You are moving through a terminal and a public building. Hear the six sign surfaces once, then choose the action each one controls.

mx-b11-n01.text: A taquería may have table service, a counter, a cashier or more than one step. Do not perform a ritual you guessed from another place. First make your group visible.

mx-b11-p01.text: You and one companion arrive in the afternoon. Greet the person receiving customers and state your group size. Speak now.

mx-b11-n02.text: Group size does not promise a seat. Ask for the concrete resource you need. The number returns inside the destination: a table for two.

mx-b11-p02.text: The room is busy and no one has pointed to a seat yet. Ask whether there is a table for the two of you. Speak now.

mx-b11-n03.text: A gesture toward an open table may still leave one doubt: assigned or free. Confirm the seat before occupying it; one short question is cheaper than relocating plates and bags.

mx-b11-p03.text: You reach the open table indicated at the back. Confirm that you should sit there. Speak now.

mx-b11-n04.text: Now discover where the order begins. One question spans table service and counter service. Aquí versus en la mesa is a channel decision, not a lesson about restaurant types.

mx-b11-p04.text: There is a cashier near the entrance and menus on the tables. Ask where your order should start. Speak now.

mx-b11-r04.text: Aquí en la caja, por favor.

mx-b11-n05.text: The channel is known. Buy time with the first drink while you look at the food. Un goes before agua here because the first sound is stressed; keep the whole useful phrase rather than carrying the rule.

mx-b11-p05.text: At the correct ordering point, ask for one sparkling water before choosing food. Speak now.

mx-b11-n06.text: Anything else does not force the taco decision. Close only this round and keep the menu open. Por ahora means for now; it leaves the next order alive.

mx-b11-t06.text: Eso es todo por ahora, gracias.

mx-b11-p06.text: You have the first drink but still need time with the menu. Close this round without closing the whole meal. Speak now.

mx-b11-s01.text: ¿Ordeno aquí o en la mesa? Un agua mineral, por favor. Eso es todo por ahora, gracias.

mx-b11-n07.text: B11 complete. Make the group visible. Ask for the table. Confirm the seat. Discover the ordering channel. Get the first drink. Close for now. B12 will earn the right to change the food; today the taquería has already started working for you.

mx-b11-q-i.text: Two travellers enter a busy taquería. Listen for the moment when the service format becomes clear and for the phrase that leaves the food order open.

mx-b11-q01.text: Buenas tardes. Somos dos. ¿Hay mesa para dos?

mx-b11-q03.text: ¿Nos sentamos aquí? ¿Ordeno aquí o en la mesa?

mx-b11-q04.text: Sí, adelante. Aquí en la caja, por favor.

mx-b11-q05.text: Un agua mineral, por favor. Eso es todo por ahora, gracias.

mx-b12-n01.text: B11 found the ordering channel. Now the menu gives you the base and six small controls change the result. Start with quantity and the item exactly as you see it.

mx-b12-t01.text: Quería dos tacos al pastor, por favor.

mx-b12-p01.text: At the cashier from B11, order two of the rotating-spit tacos named on the menu. Speak now.

mx-b12-n02.text: Todo is not a national ingredient list. Answer with the ingredients you want. First taco: con carries the additions printed or visible here.

mx-b12-p02.text: For the first taco, accept the chopped onion and cilantro offered at this counter. Speak now.

mx-b12-n03.text: Second taco, different build. Sin removes one named ingredient; it does not certify allergy safety. B13 handles the high-stakes kitchen conversation.

mx-b12-t03.text: El otro sin cebolla, por favor.

mx-b12-p03.text: Your companion wants the second taco without the chopped onion. Change only that taco. Speak now.

mx-b12-n04.text: Keep the salsa reversible. Aparte moves it beside the taco, so you control the first taste instead of asking the kitchen to guess your heat limit.

mx-b12-p04.text: Ask for the salsa in a separate small container, not poured over either taco. Speak now.

mx-b12-n05.text: Red and green name ingredients or appearance, not a reliable heat ladder. Ask the comparison that matters and follow the person’s gesture to this batch.

mx-b12-p05.text: Two unlabelled salsas are beside the tacos. Ask which one is less spicy. Speak now.

mx-b12-n06.text: Más asks for one visible addition, not an undefined bigger portion. Point to the lime wedges and name the thing you want more of.

mx-b12-p06.text: The tray has one lime wedge for two tacos. Ask for more lime. Speak now.

mx-b12-n07.text: The same sin frame changes the drink. Name the whole drink, then remove the ice. This is preference control, not a health guarantee about water or preparation.

mx-b12-t07.text: Una limonada sin hielo, por favor.

mx-b12-p07.text: Add one lemonade but ask for it without ice. Speak now.

mx-b12-s01.text: Uno con cebolla y cilantro. El otro sin cebolla. La salsa aparte. Más limón. Una limonada sin hielo.

mx-b12-n08.text: B12 complete. Order the base from the menu. Con adds. Sin removes a named preference. Aparte keeps salsa reversible. Ask which batch is less spicy. Más adds the visible thing. Sin changes the drink too. Allergy is not a preference and gets its own protected route next.

mx-b12-q-i.text: A pair orders two tacos from the same base but wants different toppings. Listen for the return question and for every control that follows.

mx-b12-q01.text: Quería dos tacos al pastor, por favor.

mx-b12-q03.text: Uno con cebolla y cilantro. El otro sin cebolla, por favor.

mx-b12-q04.text: La salsa aparte, por favor. ¿Cuál salsa pica menos?

mx-b12-q06.text: Más limón, por favor. Una limonada sin hielo.

mx-b13-n01.text: Start with yesterday’s reversible request. Salsa beside the taco lets you test before adding it. Today the stakes change: preference becomes allergy, and the safest tool is not a clever sentence. It is a fixed warning plus a written card that reaches the person preparing the food.

mx-b13-p01.text: Recall B12. Ask for the salsa on the side. Speak now.

mx-b13-n02.text: Now freeze the warning. Do not soften grave, and do not replace alergia with a preference. This example uses peanut. Your real card must name your own allergen before the trip.

mx-b13-t01.text: Tengo una alergia grave al cacahuate.

mx-b13-p02.text: Before ordering, state the severe peanut allergy without adding a long explanation. Speak now.

mx-b13-p03.text: The server asks which food. Say that you cannot eat anything containing peanut. Speak now.

mx-b13-t02.text: No puedo comer nada que contenga cacahuate.

mx-b13-n03.text: Speech opens the conversation; the card carries the exact warning into the kitchen. Hand it over and ask for the person preparing the food to see it. A nod at the table is not kitchen confirmation.

mx-b13-t03.text: ¿Puede mostrarle esta tarjeta a la persona que prepara la comida?

mx-b13-p04.text: Place the allergy card in the server’s hand and ask for it to reach the person preparing the food. Speak now.

mx-b13-r02.text: Voy a preguntarle a la cocina.

mx-b13-n04.text: Ingredient lists are only half the question. Shared oil, surfaces and utensils can carry the allergen. Ask about the concrete path, not the technical term alone.

mx-b13-t04.text: ¿Se prepara en la misma superficie o con los mismos utensilios?

mx-b13-p05.text: The server returns but has only checked the ingredient list. Ask about the same surface or utensils. Speak now.

mx-b13-n05.text: That honest answer is not a service failure. It is the information you needed. Do not bargain for a promise the kitchen cannot make. End the order and leave.

mx-b13-t05.text: Entonces no voy a comer aquí.

mx-b13-p06.text: The kitchen uses the same surface. Protect the decision: say you will not eat here. Speak now.

mx-b13-n06.text: Uncertainty gets the same decision. If the person cannot confirm the ingredients or preparation path, thank them for being honest and do not take the risk. Keep prescribed medication and the emergency plan accessible; this lesson does not replace either.

mx-b13-t06.text: Gracias por decírmelo. No voy a arriesgarme.

mx-b13-p07.text: The answer is ‘I’m not sure.’ Thank the person for saying so and refuse the risk. Speak now.

mx-b13-s01.text: Tengo una alergia grave al cacahuate. ¿Puede mostrarle esta tarjeta a la persona que prepara la comida? ¿Se prepara en la misma superficie o con los mismos utensilios?

mx-b13-n07.text: B13 complete. Preference is reversible; severe allergy is not. You froze the warning, sent a written card to the kitchen, asked about shared surfaces and utensils, and left on an unsafe or uncertain answer. Before travel, replace peanut with your actual allergen and review the card and emergency plan with your clinician.

mx-b13-q-i.text: The kitchen gives an honest answer about a shared surface. Listen for the warning, the concrete preparation question and the safe decision.

mx-b13-q01.text: Tengo una alergia grave al cacahuate.

mx-b13-q03.text: No puedo comer nada que contenga cacahuate.

mx-b13-q04.text: ¿Puede mostrarle esta tarjeta a la persona que prepara la comida?

mx-b13-q05.text: Voy a preguntarle a la cocina.

mx-b13-q06.text: ¿Se prepara en la misma superficie o con los mismos utensilios?

mx-b13-q08.text: Entonces no voy a comer aquí.

mx-b14-n01.text: Recall the first-hour payment question. Before leaving the airport you asked whether card worked. Bring that question to the restaurant now, but do not let the terminal outrun the bill.

mx-b14-p01.text: Recall B06. Before ordering, ask whether you can pay by card. Speak now.

mx-b14-n02.text: The meal is finished. Ask for the bill before asking for the terminal. The paper or screen gives you something you can inspect.

mx-b14-p02.text: The plates are clear but no bill has arrived. Ask for it. Speak now.

mx-b14-n03.text: Prices in a Mexican restaurant should be shown in pesos and include taxes. You do not need to produce a spoken number from memory. Ask for the total, then ask to see it if the answer runs past your ear.

mx-b14-p03.text: The bill has several lines. Ask for the final amount. Speak now.

mx-b14-p04.text: You did not catch the amount. Do not guess or practise arithmetic aloud; ask to see it. Speak now.

mx-b14-n04.text: Your finger stops on a line you did not choose. Do not accuse and do not pay first. Ask what the charge is. If it is a tip added without your consent, name the missing authorisation and ask for removal.

mx-b14-p05.text: There is an extra line on the bill. Point to it and ask what it is. Speak now.

mx-b14-t05.text: No autoricé este cargo. ¿Puede quitarlo, por favor?

mx-b14-p06.text: The server says the unrequested line is the tip. State that you did not authorise it and ask for removal. Speak now.

mx-b14-n05.text: Removing an unauthorised line does not forbid a voluntary tip. Choose your own amount after the corrected total. This lesson gives no universal percentage: service, setting and your decision vary. If speaking the number is fragile, show the amount on your phone.

mx-b14-t06.text: Quiero agregar esta cantidad de propina.

mx-b14-p07.text: The corrected bill is in front of you. Show the amount you chose on your phone and say you want to add that amount as a tip. Speak now.

mx-b14-n06.text: Now the total is the total you approved. Ask for the terminal to come to you, compare the amount on its screen with the corrected bill, then pay.

mx-b14-p08.text: The corrected bill is ready and you are keeping the card with you. Ask for the terminal. Speak now.

mx-b14-n07.text: Close the loop with evidence. Ask for the receipt and keep it until the charge appears correctly. The receipt is not clutter; it is the last checkable artifact in the scene.

mx-b14-t08.text: ¿Me puede dar el recibo, por favor?

mx-b14-p09.text: Payment went through. Ask for the receipt before you leave. Speak now.

mx-b14-s01.text: ¿Me trae la cuenta, por favor? ¿Cuál es el total? ¿Qué es este cargo? ¿Me trae la terminal, por favor?

mx-b14-n08.text: B14 complete. Bill before terminal. Total visible instead of guessed. Unknown line identified. Unauthorised tip removed. Your own tip chosen without a universal percentage. Terminal amount compared, receipt kept. You authorised the payment instead of merely completing it.

mx-b14-q-i.text: A traveller receives a bill with an extra tip line before the card terminal arrives. Listen for the review sequence and the amount that is actually authorised.

mx-b14-q05.text: No autoricé este cargo. ¿Puede quitarlo, por favor?

mx-b14-q07.text: Quiero agregar esta cantidad de propina. ¿Me trae la terminal, por favor?

mx-b15-n01.text: Recall the artifact that closed B14. A restaurant receipt verifies one payment; a shop receipt may need to travel back with the product. Ask for it again before the shopping scene begins.

mx-b15-p01.text: Recall B14. The card payment is complete. Ask for the receipt. Speak now.

mx-b15-c01.text: ¿Me puede dar el recibo, por favor?

mx-b15-n02.text: At a clothing shop, point before you name. Esta camisa makes one visible item the centre of the question; the price becomes a return you can ask to see.

mx-b15-p02.text: A shirt has no visible price. Point to it and ask the cost. Speak now.

mx-b15-n03.text: The label says your usual size, but the garment itself is the evidence. Ask for a larger size, then ask to try it on. Size systems and brands vary; fit wins over the letter on the tag.

mx-b15-p03.text: The shirt on the rack is tight across the shoulders. Ask for a larger size. Speak now.

mx-b15-p04.text: The larger shirt is in your hand. Ask whether you can try it on. Speak now.

mx-b15-r03.text: Sí. Los probadores están al fondo.

mx-b15-n04.text: The second shirt hangs loose. Do not translate a size chart. Ask for the direction the garment needs to move: una talla más chica.

mx-b15-p05.text: The shirt now hangs too loose. Ask for one size smaller. Speak now.

mx-b15-n05.text: The third size works. Close the choice with me llevo esta: this visible one, not a catalogue of colours or sizes.

mx-b15-p06.text: This size fits and you want the shirt in your hand. Say you will take this one. Speak now.

mx-b15-n06.text: Fit is not the same as a defect, so do not assume the exchange rule. Before paying, ask whether you can change it if the fit fails later, then ask how many days the store gives you.

mx-b15-t06.text: ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda?

mx-b15-p07.text: Before paying, ask whether the shirt can be exchanged later if the fit is wrong. Speak now.

mx-b15-r06.text: Sí, con el recibo y la etiqueta.

mx-b15-p08.text: The store accepts the exchange with receipt and tag, but you still need the deadline. Ask how many days you have. Speak now.

mx-b15-n07.text: The next morning, the fit is wrong under real movement. The tag is still attached and the receipt is in your hand. Ask for another size; the clerk asks for the two artifacts the store named.

mx-b15-p09.text: You return with the shirt. Ask to exchange it for another size. Speak now.

mx-b15-p10.text: The clerk asks for the receipt and tag. Put both on the counter and answer. Speak now.

mx-b15-s01.text: ¿Cuánto cuesta esta camisa? ¿Me la puedo probar? ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda? Quiero cambiarla por otra talla.

mx-b15-n08.text: B15 complete. Price visible. Fit tested instead of translated. Larger and smaller sizes requested by direction. Exchange policy and deadline asked before payment. Receipt and tag preserved. The return to the counter now has a sentence and the evidence the store requested.

mx-b15-q-i.text: A traveller tries three sizes, asks the exchange rule before paying and returns with the two artifacts the store requested.

mx-b15-q02.text: Sí. Los probadores están al fondo.

mx-b15-q03.text: ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda?

mx-b15-q04.text: Sí, con el recibo y la etiqueta.

mx-b16-n01.text: Recall B04. Before flying, you made the reservation portable. At reception, open that same booking with the name attached; then improve the room before its number is printed.

mx-b16-p01.text: The receptionist looks up from the screen. State that you have a reservation under the name Morgan. Speak now.

mx-b16-c01.text: Tengo una reservación a nombre de Morgan.

mx-b16-n02.text: The room is not assigned yet. Ask for the outcome that matters, not a magic room number: una habitación más silenciosa.

mx-b16-p02.text: Before the key is issued, ask whether a quieter room is available. Speak now.

mx-b16-r02.text: Sí, tengo una lejos del elevador.

mx-b16-n03.text: Quiet has been answered. If height matters too, ask separately so the receptionist can tell you what is actually available.

mx-b16-t02.text: ¿Tiene una habitación en un piso alto?

mx-b16-p03.text: The quiet room is available. Ask whether it can also be on a high floor. Speak now.

mx-b16-n04.text: Now ask the time-sensitive extra before the final morning. Late checkout is availability and policy, not an entitlement; the answer may include a limit or charge.

mx-b16-p04.text: Your flight leaves late tomorrow. Ask whether a later checkout is possible. Speak now.

mx-b16-r04.text: Sí, hasta las dos, con un cargo adicional.

mx-b16-p05.text: Late checkout is available with an extra charge. Ask its cost before accepting. Speak now.

mx-b16-n05.text: Upstairs, the room is quiet but the air conditioner does not start. Name the object and the observable failure. One clean sentence gets maintenance moving.

mx-b16-p06.text: The room is quiet, but the air conditioner will not start. Report the observable failure. Speak now.

mx-b16-n06.text: A promise without a time leaves you waiting. Ask when someone can check it. You are not demanding a universal service time; you are turning this repair into a checkpoint.

mx-b16-p07.text: Reception will send maintenance. Ask when they can check the unit. Speak now.

mx-b16-n07.text: The checkpoint passes and the unit still does not work. Now escalate one level: state that the failure continues and ask for another room. The request is earned by the unresolved scene, not opened as a threat.

mx-b16-t07.text: Sigue sin funcionar. Necesito otra habitación, por favor.

mx-b16-p08.text: Maintenance checked the unit, but it still does not work. State that and ask for another room. Speak now.

mx-b16-r07.text: Entiendo. Le voy a cambiar la habitación.

mx-b16-s01.text: ¿Hay una habitación más silenciosa? ¿Es posible salir más tarde mañana? El aire acondicionado no funciona. Necesito otra habitación, por favor.

mx-b16-n08.text: B16 complete. Reservation opened. Quiet and high floor requested before assignment. Late checkout and its charge checked. Defect named without drama. Repair given a time. Another room requested only after the checkpoint failed. You improved first and repaired second.

mx-b16-q-i.text: A traveller improves the room before assignment, then reports one defect and escalates only after the promised repair checkpoint fails.

mx-b16-q02.text: Sí, tengo una lejos del elevador.

mx-b16-q07.text: Sigue sin funcionar. Necesito otra habitación, por favor.

mx-b17-n01.text: This is the one part of the whole module that is openly defensive. Most of it stays small: a headache, a question at the pharmacy counter. But the same four moves scale up to a real emergency, so we build them here, while the stakes are still low.

mx-b17-p01.text: At the pharmacy counter, name the pain before asking for anything. Speak now.

mx-b17-n02.text: Duration is the first thing a pharmacist actually needs, not a diagnosis. Keep it to one clean answer.

mx-b17-p02.text: The pharmacist asks since when. Answer with one clean phrase: since yesterday. Speak now.

mx-b17-r02.text: Le recomiendo este para el dolor.

mx-b17-n03.text: Here is the wall. Since 2010, a Mexican pharmacy cannot sell an antibiotic without a prescription from a doctor licensed in Mexico — and a prescription from your own country will not be accepted at this counter. Asking first saves you an argument you cannot win.

mx-b17-p03.text: Before you take anything to the till, ask whether this medication needs a prescription. Speak now.

mx-b17-n04.text: One more filter before you buy, and it connects back to B13. If you have an allergy, the pharmacy counter is not exempt from that sentence.

mx-b17-t04.text: Tengo una alergia. ¿Tiene algo sin aspirina?

mx-b17-p04.text: You cannot take aspirin. Say so and ask for an alternative. Speak now.

mx-b17-n05.text: Now the scale-up. Same four moves — name it, give it a timeframe, ask the constraint, get the answer — but the object is a real emergency, and the phone is the counter.

mx-b17-p05.text: Someone next to you has collapsed. Call and say you need an ambulance. Speak now.

mx-b17-n06.text: 911 is the number for the whole country: ambulance, police and fire, all through the same door. Give the address you already made portable back in B04 — this is exactly what it was for.

mx-b17-p06.text: Give your location using the hotel name and room number. Speak now.

mx-b17-t06.text: Estoy en el hotel, en la habitación trescientos cinco.

mx-b17-s01.text: Me duele la cabeza. ¿Necesito receta para este medicamento? Necesito una ambulancia.

mx-b17-n07.text: B17 complete. Name the problem. Give it a timeframe if asked. Ask the constraint before you hit it — receta, alergia. And if it scales up: 911, the ambulance, the address you already had ready. The only defensive part of the module, and now it is four short moves, not a fear.

mx-b17-q-i.text: A traveller describes a headache at the pharmacy, checks the prescription rule and later calls for real help. Listen for the same four-move pattern at two different scales.

mx-b17-q01.text: Me duele la cabeza. Desde ayer.

mx-b17-q02.text: Le recomiendo este para el dolor.

mx-b17-q05.text: Necesito una ambulancia. Estoy en el hotel, en la habitación trescientos cinco.

mx-b18-n01.text: Last morning. The flight is hours away but the room is not. Close the room properly, store the bag somewhere real, thank the people who made the stay work, and leave the same way you arrived — with a sentence, not a silent exit.

mx-b18-r01.text: Buenos días. ¿Todo bien con la habitación?

mx-b18-p01.text: Reception asks how the room was. Confirm and say you're here to check out. Speak now.

mx-b18-t01.text: Todo bien, gracias. Vengo a hacer el check-out.

mx-b18-n02.text: The flight is late tonight and the checkout clock does not care. Do not carry the bag around the city all day. Ask the one question that solves it.

mx-b18-t02.text: ¿Puedo dejar mi maleta aquí hasta la tarde?

mx-b18-p02.text: Your flight isn't until tonight. Ask whether you can leave your suitcase here until the afternoon. Speak now.

mx-b18-r03.text: Sí, claro. Aquí tiene su comprobante.

mx-b18-n03.text: Hold onto that comprobante. It is the same logic as the receipts in B14 and B15: the small paper that gets your bag back without an argument at the desk later.

mx-b18-r04.text: ¿Le gustaría dejar alguna propina para la camarista?

mx-b18-n04.text: This one is genuinely voluntary, unlike the automatic line B14 taught you to question. A common local practice is a small amount left visibly in the room each day, since the person who cleans can change daily — but the choice and the amount are yours.

mx-b18-t03.text: Sí, ya la dejé en la habitación.

mx-b18-p03.text: You already left a tip in the room this morning. Confirm that. Speak now.

mx-b18-n05.text: Last piece, and it costs one sentence. Not a review, not a summary of the trip — just the same close you used all module: thanks, and see you.

mx-b18-r05.text: Gracias por su visita. Que tenga buen viaje.

mx-b18-p04.text: Close the stay the way you closed every counter this trip. Thank them and say goodbye. Speak now.

mx-b18-s01.text: Vengo a hacer el check-out. ¿Puedo dejar mi maleta aquí hasta la tarde? Muchas gracias. Hasta luego.

mx-b18-n06.text: B18 complete, and básico with it. Check out, store the bag with a real claim ticket, decide the tip on your own terms, and close with the same two words you opened every counter with. You did not just survive the day — you ran it, from ho-TEL to hasta luego.

mx-b18-q-i.text: A traveller checks out hours before a night flight. Listen for the storage ticket, the voluntary tip and the final goodbye.

mx-b18-q01.text: Todo bien, gracias. Vengo a hacer el check-out.

mx-b18-q02.text: ¿Puedo dejar mi maleta aquí hasta la tarde?

mx-b18-q03.text: Sí, claro. Aquí tiene su comprobante.

mx-b18-q04.text: ¿Le gustaría dejar alguna propina para la camarista?

mx-b18-q05.text: Sí, ya la dejé en la habitación.

mx-i01-n01.text: Part one of the good stuff. Today's decision is not a phrase — it's a time. What hour you sit down decides which room you eat in, and the two rooms are not the same trip.

mx-i01-n02.text: Six in the evening, and the whole comedor is yours — every table free, the cook visible through the kitchen door, nobody else in the room.

mx-i01-n03.text: Nothing has gone wrong. La comida — the main meal — runs one to three. By six, the city already ate hours ago; what's open now is running on tourist hours, not local ones.

mx-i01-p01.text: You want to know when this place is genuinely busy. Ask what time la comida is usually served here. Speak now.

mx-i01-t01.text: ¿A qué hora sirven la comida aquí?

mx-i01-r02.text: De una a tres, más o menos.

mx-i01-n04.text: Now the other end of the day. Cena is not a second comida — it runs later and lighter, sometimes just something from a stall, not a sit-down production.

mx-i01-t02.text: Para la cena, algo ligero está bien.

mx-i01-p02.text: It's evening and you're not looking for a full meal. Say something light is fine for dinner. Speak now.

mx-i01-n05.text: So the move: if you want the room the city actually eats in, walk in for comida between one and three. If you just want something before bed, cena any time after six is completely normal.

mx-i01-r03.text: ¿Va a comer aquí o solo va de paso?

mx-i01-p03.text: You've arrived right in the middle of la comida. Say you'd like to eat, here, now. Speak now.

mx-i01-t03.text: Sí, quiero comer aquí, por favor.

mx-i01-s01.text: ¿A qué hora sirven la comida aquí? Para la cena, algo ligero está bien.

mx-i01-n06.text: I01 complete. Comida owns one to three — that's the room worth walking into. Cena is real but lighter, any time after six. An empty comedor at six isn't a warning sign. It's the clock telling you exactly where you are.

mx-i01-q-i.text: A traveller walks into an empty comedor at six in the evening and asks when it actually fills up.

mx-i01-q02.text: ¿A qué hora sirven la comida aquí?

mx-i01-q03.text: De una a tres, más o menos.

mx-i01-q04.text: Para la cena, algo ligero está bien.

mx-i02-n01.text: A busy counter in Mexico often has no formal line at all — just a cluster of people, and whoever makes eye contact and speaks up gets served next. Standing back quietly, the way you might queue at home, can mean waiting a very long time.

mx-i02-n02.text: You're the fourth person deep at a busy taco stand, no line, everyone talking over everyone. The cook glances up. This is the half-second that matters.

mx-i02-n03.text: That question is your opening, not a formality to survive. Answer it immediately, at a normal speaking volume — not a whisper, not a shout.

mx-i02-p01.text: The cook asks who's next. Claim your turn immediately. Speak now.

mx-i02-n04.text: If two people speak at once and it isn't clear who was actually first, this line settles it without an argument.

mx-i02-p02.text: Someone else also claims the turn. Say, calmly, that you think you arrived first. Speak now.

mx-i02-n05.text: Here's the permission this whole part is built on. The English instinct — 'I was wondering if I could possibly...' — doesn't read as polite here. It reads as distance, and it makes the cook wonder if you're actually ready to order.

mx-i02-p03.text: Order directly, no padding, no apology for existing. Speak now.

mx-i02-t03.text: Deme dos de pastor, por favor.

mx-i02-s01.text: Yo sigo, por favor. Creo que yo llegué primero. Deme dos de pastor, por favor.

mx-i02-n06.text: I02 complete. No formal line, no problem: yo sigo claims your turn, creo que yo llegué primero defends it if needed, and a direct deme plus what you want is the whole order. Quiet waiting was never the polite move — speaking up, at a normal volume, was.

mx-i02-q-i.text: A crowded taco stand with no formal line. Listen for how the traveller claims a turn and orders directly.

mx-i02-q04.text: Deme dos de pastor, por favor.

mx-i03-n01.text: Some of the best food in Mexico has no printed menu at all. It has a chalkboard, or nothing — just today's comida corrida, decided in the kitchen that morning.

mx-i03-r01.text: Hoy tenemos comida corrida: sopa, guisado y agua.

mx-i03-n02.text: Comida corrida — the same idea as a menú del día — is a full, fixed multi-course lunch at a fair price, usually only available for a few hours around midday. It's not a limited option. It's often the actual reason to be there.

mx-i03-p01.text: That's exactly what you want. Say you'll have the comida corrida. Speak now.

mx-i03-t01.text: Quiero la comida corrida, por favor.

mx-i03-n03.text: Comida corrida still asks you to choose between two or three set options at each course. You don't need every word — you need one clean choice.

mx-i03-p02.text: Pick one. Say soup. Speak now.

mx-i03-n04.text: And when there genuinely is a longer menu and no comida corrida in sight, this is the move that unlocks the good dish instead of the safe one.

mx-i03-p03.text: You're not sure what to get. Ask what they recommend. Speak now.

mx-i03-s01.text: Quiero la comida corrida, por favor. ¿Qué me recomienda?

mx-i03-n05.text: I03 complete. Comida corrida is the move, not the fallback — a full fixed lunch, fair price, usually the best thing in the room. And when there's a longer menu instead, ¿qué me recomienda? gets you today's actual best dish, not just the one you already knew the name of.

mx-i03-q-i.text: A fonda with no printed menu. Listen for how the traveller orders the fixed daily lunch and asks for a recommendation elsewhere.

mx-i03-q01.text: Hoy tenemos comida corrida: sopa, guisado y agua.

mx-i03-q02.text: Quiero la comida corrida, por favor.

mx-i04-n01.text: Tonight's decision happens before a single drink is ordered, in one word: who invited whom. That answer already decides who reaches for the bill later, and knowing it now avoids an awkward tug-of-war at the end.

mx-i04-r01.text: Vamos por unas cervezas, yo invito.

mx-i04-n02.text: Yo invito isn't a small offer to be politely refused three times. It's a plain statement of who's paying tonight — and the expected answer is thanks, not a fight over the bill.

mx-i04-p01.text: A friend says he's inviting. Accept it plainly, with thanks. Speak now.

mx-i04-n03.text: But you're allowed to want the other arrangement. Splitting is not the default here — so if you want it, say so early, clearly, before the tab starts running.

mx-i04-p02.text: You'd rather split the bill this time. Say so, before ordering. Speak now.

mx-i04-n04.text: One more version, for a group that's fine sharing a table but not a tab: everyone pays for what they actually had.

mx-i04-p03.text: Suggest that everyone pays for their own order. Speak now.

mx-i04-n05.text: And when the night's done and you're leaving before the rest of the table, the exit doesn't need a speech. One line covers it.

mx-i04-p04.text: You're heading out while the others stay. Say goodbye to the table. Speak now.

mx-i04-t04.text: Ya me voy. Gracias por todo, nos vemos.

mx-i04-s01.text: ¿Podemos pagar por separado? Cada quien paga lo suyo. Ya me voy. Gracias por todo, nos vemos.

mx-i04-n06.text: I04 complete. Yo invito means they're paying — accept it. If you'd rather split, say ¿podemos pagar por separado? early. And when you're the one leaving first, ya me voy plus a thank-you closes it cleanly, no drawn-out goodbye required.

mx-i04-q-i.text: A night out with friends. Listen for who pays, how splitting is requested, and how to leave the table first.

mx-i04-q01.text: Vamos por unas cervezas, yo invito.

mx-i04-q04.text: Ya me voy. Gracias por todo, nos vemos.

mx-i05-n01.text: Almost every stranger who talks to you will ask some version of the same four or five questions. That's good news — it means you can walk in with real answers ready, instead of building each one from scratch under pressure.

mx-i05-p01.text: Answer with where you're actually from. Speak now.

mx-i05-n02.text: This one wants a real number, not a philosophy. Keep it short.

mx-i05-p02.text: Give your real length of stay. Speak now.

mx-i05-r03.text: ¿Qué te ha gustado más de México?

mx-i05-n03.text: This is the question that makes the conversation warm instead of transactional. A specific answer lands better than a generic 'everything' — it shows you were actually paying attention.

mx-i05-p03.text: Give one specific thing you've genuinely liked. Speak now.

mx-i05-t03.text: Me encantó la comida, sobre todo los tacos.

mx-i05-p04.text: Say who you're travelling with, or that you're on your own. Speak now.

mx-i05-n04.text: And if you want out of a conversation, that's fine too — one polite line closes it without rudeness.

mx-i05-p05.text: You need to get going. Excuse yourself politely. Speak now.

mx-i05-t05.text: Bueno, fue un gusto. Que le vaya bien.

mx-i05-s01.text: Soy de Estados Unidos. Diez días, más o menos. Me encantó la comida.

mx-i05-n05.text: I05 complete. Origin, duration, what you've liked, who you're with — the same four questions, almost every time. Have your real answers ready, and the fifth skill, leaving a conversation politely, is just as useful as staying in one.

mx-i05-q-i.text: A friendly stranger asks the same handful of questions travellers hear constantly. Listen for the ready answers and the polite exit.

mx-i05-q03.text: ¿Qué te ha gustado más de México?

mx-i05-q04.text: Me encantó la comida, sobre todo los tacos.

mx-i06-n01.text: Everything so far has lived in the present: order this, ask that, right now. Today the trip gets a past tense — three verbs that let you tell someone what yesterday actually was.

mx-i06-n02.text: Fui — I went. The whole day starts with where you went, and that one word carries the whole sentence.

mx-i06-p01.text: Say where you went yesterday. Speak now.

mx-i06-n03.text: Comí — I ate. Same pattern, different verb. The story is building itself one short sentence at a time.

mx-i06-p02.text: Say what you ate. Speak now.

mx-i06-n04.text: And the verb that closes the story with feeling, not just fact: me encantó. It loved-me, literally — the thing did the loving, in Spanish grammar. But it lands exactly like 'I loved it.'

mx-i06-p03.text: Say you loved it. Speak now.

mx-i06-n05.text: The conversation naturally swings forward too. You don't need a new tense for tomorrow — vamos a plus what you'll do covers it.

mx-i06-p04.text: Say what you're going to do today. Speak now.

mx-i06-t04.text: Vamos a ir a la playa.

mx-i06-s01.text: Fui al mercado. Comí tacos al pastor. Me encantó.

mx-i06-n06.text: I06 complete. Fui, comí, me encantó — three verbs, and yesterday becomes a real story instead of a list of nouns. Vamos a covers tomorrow. You now have a past and a future, not just an endless present.

mx-i06-q-i.text: Someone asks about yesterday. Listen for the three verbs that carry the whole story.

mx-i06-q02.text: Fui al mercado. Comí tacos al pastor. Me encantó.

mx-i06-q04.text: Vamos a ir a la playa.

mx-i07-n01.text: Two moves today, both about saying something true out loud instead of keeping it to yourself: a genuine compliment, and a calm complaint. Both work better specific than vague.

mx-i07-n02.text: This is your opening. Está buenísimo works, but naming the actual dish gets a bigger reaction — it proves you weren't just being polite.

mx-i07-p01.text: The food was genuinely excellent. Say so, specifically. Speak now.

mx-i07-r02.text: Muchas gracias, se lo voy a decir.

mx-i07-n03.text: Now the other move. Something's actually wrong — not a preference, an actual problem. Name the object and the issue, calmly, without a speech attached.

mx-i07-p02.text: The soup arrived cold. Name the problem, calmly. Speak now.

mx-i07-r03.text: Perdón, se la cambio ahora mismo.

mx-i07-n04.text: Disculpe opens it without blame. Naming the object and the exact problem — not a general complaint — is what actually gets it fixed fast.

mx-i07-p03.text: They fixed it fast. Thank them for taking care of it. Speak now.

mx-i07-s01.text: El mole está buenísimo. Disculpe, la sopa está fría. Gracias por resolverlo tan rápido.

mx-i07-n05.text: I07 complete. A specific compliment brings the cook out to say thanks in person. A calm, specific complaint — disculpe plus the exact problem — gets it fixed fast, no confrontation required. Both moves work because they're honest and precise, not because they're loud.

mx-i07-q-i.text: A meal with one genuine compliment and one real problem. Listen for how both get handled calmly and specifically.

mx-i08-n01.text: Being invited into someone's home is a real gesture, not a formality, and three small moves make you a good guest: something small in your hands, arriving on time, and letting your host lead the first toast.

mx-i08-r01.text: ¿Te gustaría cenar en mi casa el sábado?

mx-i08-p01.text: Accept the invitation warmly. Speak now.

mx-i08-t01.text: Claro que sí, con mucho gusto.

mx-i08-n02.text: Don't arrive empty-handed. Something small — flowers, wine, a dessert — is the norm. Skip yellow flowers, which read as mourning here, not celebration.

mx-i08-p02.text: At the door, hand over the small gift you brought. Speak now.

mx-i08-t02.text: Le traje esto para la casa.

mx-i08-r02.text: No te hubieras molestado, muchas gracias.

mx-i08-n03.text: Everything else about time here can be relaxed. This isn't. Arriving on time for a home invitation reads as respect for the work someone put into tonight.

mx-i08-r03.text: Pasa, siéntete como en tu casa.

mx-i08-p03.text: Thank them for having you. Speak now.

mx-i08-n04.text: Glasses fill, and the table waits. The host leads the first toast — you don't need to invent one. When it comes, one word is the whole reply.

mx-i08-p04.text: The host raises a glass. Answer the toast. Speak now.

mx-i08-s01.text: Claro que sí, con mucho gusto. Le traje esto para la casa. Gracias por invitarme.

mx-i08-n05.text: I08 complete. Bring something small. Arrive on time — this is the one place the relaxed clock doesn't apply. Let the host lead the toast, and salud covers your whole reply. Being a good guest here is three small, specific moves, not a performance.

mx-i08-q-i.text: A traveller is invited to dinner at a friend's home. Listen for the gift, the timing, and the toast.

mx-i08-q01.text: ¿Te gustaría cenar en mi casa el sábado?

mx-i08-q02.text: Claro que sí, con mucho gusto.

mx-i08-q03.text: Le traje esto para la casa.

mx-i09-n01.text: One question opens up a whole different kind of afternoon: not what should I see, but what's actually happening. The plaza, the local market, a neighbourhood event — the answer changes week to week, and that's exactly the point.

mx-i09-r01.text: ¿Qué van a hacer este fin de semana?

mx-i09-n02.text: Turn the question back around. This is the one that gets you invited into someone's actual plan instead of a tourist itinerary.

mx-i09-p01.text: Ask what's happening in the plaza this weekend. Speak now.

mx-i09-t01.text: ¿Hay algo en la plaza este fin de semana?

mx-i09-r02.text: Sí, hay un mercado sobre ruedas los domingos.

mx-i09-n03.text: A mercado sobre ruedas — a market that sets up on a street for one day and moves on — is a completely different rhythm from a fixed tourist market. Ask to go along, not just for directions.

mx-i09-p02.text: Ask if you can come along with them. Speak now.

mx-i09-r03.text: Claro, nos vemos a las diez.

mx-i09-n04.text: Once you're there, you're not performing tourism. You're just at the market with everyone else, so the useful sentence is the same one anyone would use.

mx-i09-p03.text: Ask the price of something at a stall, like any other customer. Speak now.

mx-i09-s01.text: ¿Hay algo en la plaza este fin de semana? ¿Puedo ir con ustedes?

mx-i09-n05.text: I09 complete. ¿Hay algo en la plaza? finds out what's actually happening. ¿Puedo ir con ustedes? turns a plan into an invitation. Once you're there, you're just a customer, not a spectator — cuánto cuesta esto works exactly the same way it does everywhere else.

mx-i09-q-i.text: A traveller discovers a Sunday roving market by asking a local what's happening, then asks to come along.

mx-i09-q01.text: ¿Qué van a hacer este fin de semana?

mx-i09-q02.text: ¿Hay algo en la plaza este fin de semana?

mx-i09-q03.text: Sí, hay un mercado sobre ruedas los domingos.

mx-i10-n01.text: Today's real skill isn't the bargaining phrases — it's knowing where they belong. Get that part right, and the rest is easy and even fun.

mx-i10-n02.text: A craft stall with no price tag, no cash register, no receipt — that's an invitation to negotiate. A supermarket or a chain store is not. Reading the room correctly comes first.

mx-i10-p01.text: You're at an open craft stall, no price marked. Ask a friendly opening question. Speak now.

mx-i10-n03.text: Now you make a counter-offer, friendly, not aggressive. This is a conversation, not a demand — smiling and showing genuine interest in the piece gets you further than pressure ever will.

mx-i10-p02.text: Offer a lower price, warmly. Speak now.

mx-i10-t02.text: ¿Se lo puedo dejar en trescientos cincuenta?

mx-i10-n04.text: A friendly back-and-forth like this commonly lands somewhere around thirty percent off the opening price — not a rule, just a rough shape of how these conversations tend to go.

mx-i10-n05.text: And if the answer is a flat no, that's the end of it — pushing further is the one move that actually sours the exchange. Thank them and decide whether to buy at the stated price.

mx-i10-p03.text: The vendor can't go any lower. Thank them warmly, whether or not you buy. Speak now.

mx-i10-s01.text: ¿Cuál es su mejor precio? ¿Se lo puedo dejar en trescientos cincuenta? Está bien, muchas gracias.

mx-i10-n06.text: I10 complete. First, read the room — craft stall or supermarket. If it's a stall, ¿cuál es su mejor precio? opens it, a friendly counter-offer moves it, and a warm gracias closes it either way, deal or no deal. Money doesn't need to be tense to be real.

mx-i10-q-i.text: A traveller bargains for a craft item at an open-air stall, then accepts the final price gracefully.

mx-i10-q03.text: ¿Se lo puedo dejar en trescientos cincuenta?
